title: fix(runtime): the keys and actions domains answer their 405 with an Allow header naming POST
body:
Fixes #24023

Clause-②: no

Basis for the Clause-② line: no request that was accepted becomes refused, and none that was refused becomes accepted. A refusal that already answered `405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` now also carries an `Allow: POST` header. Its status, body and `error.code` do not change.

## What changed

- `packages/runtime/src/domains/keys.ts` and `packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts`. The 405 for every verb but `POST` was `deps.error('Method not allowed', 405)`. `deps.error` returns `{ status, body }` and nothing else. That was read off its definition (`HttpDispatcher.error`, which calls `apiErrorResponse` in `error-envelope.ts`), not off the comment in `meta.ts`. Each site now builds its response by hand, in the shape `mcp.ts`, `meta.ts` and `ai.ts` already use: `status: 405`, `headers: { Allow: 'POST' }`, and the body through `buildApiError({ message, httpStatus: 405 })`. So the code stays derived (`METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`) and is not spelled. The message and the body are byte-identical to before. The anonymous-baseline statements stay the first statement of both handlers, above the 405.
- **Why `POST`.** Each domain serves `POST` alone, on every path it claims. `handleKeysRequest` never reads its path. `handleActionsRequest` checks the method before it parses the path, and its activation door (`isActionActivationWrite`) is `POST` too. Each value is one named constant (`KEYS_ALLOWED_METHODS`, `ACTIONS_ALLOWED_METHODS`).
- `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`: the `DISPATCHER_DOMAINS` ledger now counts `keys.ts` 1 to 2 hand-built responses and `actions.ts` 0 to 1. Both are kind 1 (enveloped, built by hand only for the header), each with a note. `pnpm check:route-envelope` went red without this entry, and its failure text asks for it ("raise the count and say which in `note`"). The `meta.ts` and `ai.ts` 405s raised the same ledger. **This file is outside the claim's listed file surface.** It is the declaration the gate requires for this exact change, and the report says so too.
- New pin: `packages/runtime/src/domains/keys-actions-method-not-allowed-allow.test.ts`.
- `.changeset/24023-keys-actions-405-allow.md`: `@objectstack/runtime` `patch`.
- **No shared helper.** `meta.ts` is held by another lane, so a helper could not replace all five hand-built 405s in this PR. The dispatch rule allows a helper only if it replaces every one of them.

## The sweep (Done when, third line)

`git grep -n 405 -- packages/runtime/src/domains ':!*.test.ts'` at base `aa31569b2` finds exactly two `deps.error(…, 405)` sites, `keys.ts:112` and `actions.ts:446`. The other three 405 producers already send `Allow`: `mcp.ts:183`, `meta.ts:1583` and `ai.ts:304`. The same search at head `71613b4ef` finds zero `deps.error(…, 405)` sites and five `status: 405` literals, and each of the five has a `headers: { Allow: … }` line under it. The `deps.error` calls that take their status from a variable were checked too. No producer that feeds them has a 405: the only other non-comment `405` literals in `packages/**/src` are the data door's exposure refusal (Acceptance notes) and spec constants.

## Measured on both hosts (H4)

The build is head `e614b2adb`, driven in process. A `LiteKernel` carries a fake `auth` service that answers a session only when the request has a test header. `createHonoApp({ kernel, prefix: '/api/v1' })` is driven through `app.request`. The standalone server is `HonoServerPlugin` plus `createDispatcherPlugin` over a real socket and `fetch`. Both were run with CORS left at its default and with CORS off.

| request | `createHonoApp` | standalone server |
|---|---|---|
| signed-in `GET` or `DELETE /api/v1/keys` | `405`, `Allow: POST`, domain envelope (`httpStatus: 405`) | `405`, `Allow: POST`, domain envelope |
| signed-in `GET` or `PUT /api/v1/actions/task/close` | `405`, `Allow: POST`, domain envelope | `405`, `Allow: POST`, the **adapter's** envelope (`error.details`): only `POST` is mounted, so the domain is never reached |
| anonymous `GET /api/v1/keys` | `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`, no `Allow` | `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`, no `Allow` |
| anonymous `GET /api/v1/actions/task/close` | `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`, no `Allow` | `405`, `Allow: POST`, the adapter's (see Acceptance notes) |
| `OPTIONS` on either path, CORS default | `204` from CORS | `204` from CORS |

Neither host drops a domain's `headers`. `createHonoApp`'s `toResponse` writes `result.response.headers`, and the standalone `sendResultBase` writes them after the security headers. So the producer was the domain, as the card says, and there was nothing to fix in `domain:cli`'s host code. The base answer (no `Allow` on either host's domain 405) is the filer's reading and PR #24009's. On this branch it is reproduced by the ablation below.

## Tests

- **New pin**, 7 cases. On `dispatch()`, the call both hosts make, per domain: a signed-in `GET` gets `405`, `headers.Allow === 'POST'`, `error.code` `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`, `error.httpStatus` `405`, and the body parsed against the spec's `BaseResponseSchema` / `ApiErrorSchema`. An anonymous `GET` gets `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` with no `Allow`. On the standalone socket: the keys `405` with `allow: POST` on the wire and the domain's envelope, the anonymous keys `401` with no `allow`, and the actions `405` with `allow: POST`. That last answer is the adapter's and passes at base too. It is kept so that "both hosts" is a statement about the wire for both domains.
- **Ablation** (one run, not kept). The fix was committed first. `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, nested, put both sites back to today's `return { handled: true, response: deps.error('Method not allowed', 405) };`. Evidence: keys anchor 1 to 0, blob `f6d9a5547690` to `0365f3e2c755`; actions anchor 1 to 0, blob `e15f8b9fff19` to `bda747ac32f9`. The pin then gave `Tests 3 failed | 4 passed (7)`. The 3 failures are the dispatch-level keys and actions `Allow` rows and the socket keys row, each `expected undefined to be 'POST'` or `expected null to be 'POST'`. The anonymous rows and the adapter row stayed green. Restore: blob equals HEAD for both files, and `git diff HEAD` is empty for both. The pin imports `../http-dispatcher.js` and `../dispatcher-plugin.js` from source, so no `dist/` of the mutated package sits on its resolution path.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2` at `3fbad0f81`: `Test Files 410 passed (410)`, `Tests 6287 passed | 19 skipped (6306)`. `packages/runtime` has no byte change from `3fbad0f81` to the head `71613b4ef`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`: exit 0. The test-layer program (`tsconfig.test.json`) lists the new file (`--listFiles`: 1 hit among 413 test files), and `check:test-typecheck` holds its ledger unchanged.
- `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` over the four changed code files: exit 0.
- Neighbours run with the pin, all green: `keys-every-verb.hono.integration.test.ts`, `error-envelope.conformance.test.ts` (its `handleActions(… 'GET' …)` 405 case) and `domains/anonymous-gate-actions-automation.test.ts`.
- The `repo` vitest project (`test:repo`) was not run locally. This diff touches none of its files, and CI's `Test Core` runs it.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at head `71613b4ef`, after the merge of `origin/main`, derived 84 commands. Each was run with its exit code captured before any pipe. `--ran` reconciles: `84 derived, 83 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`. The 83 that ran all exit 0.

- **NOT MEASURED: `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`.** Reason: `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3). It reads the built `dist/` of every package, 38 of them have none in this worktree, and the whole repository was not built locally. This diff changes no `exports`, no `package.json` and no build config. CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` runs it.
- `pnpm check:route-envelope` was red on the first run, at `3fbad0f81`, for the two hand-built 405s. The ledger entry above turned it green, and it is green in the final run.
- Not run: `node scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs`, because no exported symbol was renamed or removed. The local-only families `check:dev-prereqs` and `check:skill-frame-freshness` were not run either, because nothing in `packages/spec` or the skill frame was touched.
- CI check-runs were not concluded when this PR was opened.

## Acceptance notes

- **Where the card's first line and the anonymous rule meet.** `/actions` passes the anonymous decision `method` (`shouldDenyAnonymous` lets `OPTIONS` through for CORS preflight). So an anonymous `OPTIONS` reaches the actions `405`, and with this change that answer carries `Allow: POST`. Measured: this happens only on a `createHonoApp` host with CORS off. With CORS on (the default on both hosts) every `OPTIONS` is answered `204` before routing. The standalone server with CORS off already answers that same request `405` with `Allow: POST`, from the adapter. Holding `Allow` back from that one caller would leave a 405 without `Allow`, which is what the card's first "Done when" line forbids. `/keys` decides an anonymous caller without the method, so its anonymous `OPTIONS` is `401`. This is in the report's `open_questions` for the seat to rule on if it reads the rule otherwise.
- `domains/mcp.ts` at about `:174`–`:179`: the comment still says the 405s in `actions.ts` and `keys.ts` "go through `deps.error`", which this PR makes false. The fix is one comment edit, and `mcp.ts` is outside the claim's file surface. Carrier: none.
- `error-envelope.conformance.test.ts` does not list `domains/keys.ts`, `domains/actions.ts` (nor `domains/meta.ts`) in its source-scan `MODULES`. So their hand-built bodies are held by this pin's envelope parse and by `check:route-envelope`'s ledger, not by that scan. Carrier: none.
- The data door's exposure refusal is a different shape and is outside this card's `deps.error(…, 405)` search. That refusal is `405 OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`, thrown in `action-execution.ts` and answered through `deps.errorFromThrown` in `domains/data.ts`; `RestServer`'s twin is the same. It carries no `Allow`, and its `allowed` field lists API operations, not HTTP methods. Read from source, not measured on the wire. Carrier: none.
- `handleKeysRequest` never reads its path, so on a `createHonoApp` host `/api/v1/keys/ANYTHING` reaches the domain, and `Allow: POST` is accurate there. The standalone server answers `404` for any `/keys` sub-path. Read from source, not measured. Carrier: none.
- `origin/main` gained one commit (`b9ac35cbf`, CI workflows and scripts only) while this branch was open. It was merged before the final gate run so that the gate list is read from the current workflows. The merge touched no package source, so the earlier package builds stand.
